'''CPU type''' is a hardware model code identifying which Norsk Data machine a system is. It is printed on the order confirmation, entered by the installer when SINTRAN III is generated, and displayed by the {{ND-cmd|LIST-TITLE}} command on SINTRAN III/VSX systems. It is also stamped on cabinet plates and CPU labels, written together with the CPU number in the form ''type.number''. It should not be confused with two other values that are also called "CPU type" but are found automatically by the operating system.

The CPU type is '''not''' used to configure anything. No part of the SINTRAN III kernel reads it. See [[#Does the CPU type do anything?]].

== Three different things called CPU type ==

Three separate values in SINTRAN III are referred to as a "CPU type" in different documents. Only the first is ever entered by a person.

{| class="wikitable"
! Value !! Where it comes from !! Used by the operating system?
|-
| '''CPU type''' (the order-form code) || Typed at system generation, or read from the back wiring PROM on [[ND-110]] and [[ND-120]] || '''No'''
|-
| '''HWINFO(0)''' high byte || Found at every start-up by testing the hardware || '''Yes''', constantly
|-
| '''5CPUTYPE''' || Found by probing the [[ND-100]] bus for a coprocessor interface || '''Yes'''
|}

== CPU type in system generation ==

=== The order form ===

The CPU type is filled in on the SINTRAN III order form, in the customer information section. {{ND-doc|830053.3}} describes the field:

<blockquote>
'''- CPU type:''' This is the CPU type of the system. You will find the CPU type stated on your order confirmation. [...] The symbol mark generated is 33CPU.
</blockquote>

The companion field is described as:

<blockquote>
'''- CPU no.:''' The system number must be filled in. It will identify the SINTRAN III later on when a new SINTRAN III needs to be installed. The symbol mark generated is 33CPN.
</blockquote>

Both fields appear only in the customer information header. They are not among the system parameters, such as RT-PROG, SEGM, SEMAPHORE, INTERNAL DEVICE and DEVICE BUFFER, that determine the size and shape of the generated system.

=== The NEW-SYSTEM dialogue ===

When SINTRAN III is installed from diskettes, the {{ND-cmd|NEW-SYSTEM}} program asks for both values. Its sub-command for this is CPU-UPDATE, "update CPU number and CPU type". On earlier H-version distribution floppies the task had its own program, CPU-TYPE:PROG.

{{DocPreStart}}
 Checking CPU number ... Wait ...
 > Give CPU number (in decimal): 6586
 --- OK
 Checking CPU type ... Wait ...
 > Give CPU type (in decimal):
 --- OK
{{DocPreEnd}}

Answering the CPU type is optional. {{ND-doc|30.003.007}} works through an installation on two example machines, named SAMBA, an [[ND-500|ND-570/CX]] running VSX, and MAMBA, an [[ND-100]] running VSE. In the SAMBA walkthrough the installer simply presses return at the CPU type prompt, and the manual notes:

<blockquote>
If ND has given you a CPU type (see your SINTRAN order), then you must give this as input here! The CR given above means that no CPU type was assigned for SAMBA!
</blockquote>

So a machine could be delivered with no CPU type assigned to it at all. The CPU number prompt is not optional in the same dialogue, and the manual marks the number entered as "the correct CPU number for SAMBA".

Three patterns can be seen in the numbering:

* A trailing 1 or 3 on the ND-5000 codes marks the '''SCSI''' version of the same system, for example 5430 against 5431, and 5800 against 5803.
* '''Compact''' systems have their own block of numbers, separate from the full system, for example 5791 and 5795 against 5700 and 5703.
* The last digit of an ND-5900 code is the '''number of processors''', 5902, 5903 and 5904 for two, three and four CPUs.

The two digits are also carried in the CPU number itself. The system number is usually of the form tttt.nnnnn, where tttt is the computer type or model and nnnnn is the CPU number proper.

=== Where the value is stored ===

The generation symbol is '''33CPU''', and the CPU number is '''33CPN'''. The patch and install mode file assigns the symbol into the system information array:

{{DocPreStart}}
 HWINF+2/ 33CPU
{{DocPreEnd}}

The value ends up in word 3 of the system information array, HWINFO(2). It is documented in {{ND-doc|820023.1}} as "system type (100, 102, 500, 502, 5561..)" and is returned by monitor call MON 262 in bytes 6 and 7 of the second parameter.

On an [[ND-110]] or [[ND-120]] the value is overwritten at every start-up from the back wiring PROM, if that PROM is programmed. The same PROM also carries the CPU number and the number of legal users.

=== Codes on real machines ===

The [[:Category:Individual systems|preserved machines]] confirm the numbering, and the convention of writing the two values together as ''type.number'' is found on the hardware itself. A handwritten label inside the front door of an ND-110 Satellite reads:

{{DocPreStart}}
 ORD: 20.6578 E
 CPU: 9883.21005
{{DocPreEnd}}

Cabinet plates on an ND-5800 carry the same system number on both crates, each plate naming the function of its own crate:

{{DocPreStart}}
 ND-5000 crate / Cabinet assy 1.2 / Function : MPM 5/5800 CX / System no. : 5800.21284
 ND-100 crate  / Cabinet assy 1.1 / Function : ND-120 CX     / System no. : 5800.21284
{{DocPreEnd}}

A paper order book for a Satellite writes the pair with no separator: "CPU-NO.: 900135", meaning type 900 and number 135.

Five codes are known from surviving machines that are not in the order manual's list, which the manual itself describes as only "some common values": '''900''' (NORD-100 Satellite 9, an older and shorter code predating the four-digit scheme), '''3051''', '''3392''', '''5171''' (an [[ND-500|ND-530/CX]], so the classic ND-500 family uses codes in a 51xx band) and '''5282'''. All five are in the table above.

A further 32 codes appear against real machines in the sintran.com system register but have no matching manual entry or product sheet, so what they are is not known: 10, 100, 102, 103, 500, 502, 503, 563, 570, 572, 573, 3031, 3035, 3082, 3092, 3209, 5025, 5161, 5221, 5362, 5400, 5408, 5421, 5481, 5715, 5762, 5782, 5792, 5850, 9724, 9801, 9804.


=== What every ND-110 Compact shares  ===

From the ND-110 Compact Series product sheet. The sheet carries '''no document
number and no date''' - the back page, where ND normally prints them, was not
scanned.

{| class="wikitable"
! Item !! Value
|-
| CPU and MMU || On one card, "which results in one extra free position for memory expansion". Both CPUs "totally compatible with the ND-100 CPU"
|-
| ND-110/CX gain || "approximately '''twice the performance''' of the ND-110 CPU"
|-
| Memory || 1 MB fitted, ceiling '''16 MB'''. Boards in steps of 1/2, 1 and 2 MB. 22 bits per 16-bit word, single-bit correcting
|-
| Cache || 8 KB
|-
| MMU || 16-bit virtual to '''24-bit physical''', "extending the latter from 128 KB to 32 MB". 16 page index tables of 64 words. '''Page size 2048 bytes'''
|-
| Interrupts || 16 priority levels, context switch '''3.4 us'''
|-
| Floating point || 48-bit standard (32-bit mantissa, 16-bit exponent); 32-bit optional
|-
| Rack || '''12 positions''', 8 free (7 on model 14)
|-
| Terminals || Up to '''48''', "limited only by space in the 12 position rack". No per-model interface count is given
|-
| Disk ceiling || Two 74 MB internal, up to '''1800 MB''' external
|-
| Cabinet || 69 cm high, 76 cm deep, 54 cm wide, about 78 kg, forced air
|-
| Power || Max 800 W, 230 V 50 Hz. Start peak 60 A for 30 ms, 6 A slow main fuse
|-
| Built in || Telefix adaptor, with a printer outlet for hardcopy of Telefix communication
|-

'''The model digit is the disk configuration and nothing else''' - the sheet's own
words: "four models with internal disk storage ranging from 28 MB in Model 11 to
two 74 MB disks in Model 13, and an SMD controller for external disks in Model
14." CPU, memory and floppy are identical across all four.

'''On the disk interface''': the sheet says only '''"Winchester"''' for the internal
disks and never names a controller standard. '''ST-506 and SCSI are never
mentioned'''; SMD appears only for model 14's *external* disks. So this sheet does
not settle the internal interface on its own - see the ST-506 discussion above.

'''An artefact worth knowing''': the software section opens "The following software
is delivered with the '''ND-100''' COMPACT system", and its whole documentation list
is ND-100 Compact material. The sheet was clearly set from the earlier ND-100
Compact sheet and the references were not updated.

'''Open question''': ND named these Compact models '''11, 12, 13, 14''' here, but the
order manual names Compact models '''A0, A1, B''' with a different code block
(3080/3081/3085 and 3090/3091/3095). Whether those are two generations of the
range or two naming conventions for the same machines is '''not established'''. '''[?]'''
|}

=== The 3xxx blocks ===

The 3xxx codes are not one sequence. Grouped by the second digit they match the documents:

{| class="wikitable"
! Block !! What is documented in it
|-
| 308x / 309x || ND-110 Compact A0/A1/B and ND-110/CX Compact A0/A1/B (order manual, 1988)
|-
| 320x / 327x || FTX for Compact: 3201/3202 packages, 3270 a complete ND-110 Compact/FTX
|-
| 326x || ND-100 Compact models I to IV (parts catalogue, 1984)
|-
| 329x || ND-100 Compact models 11 to 14 (parts catalogue, 1987), which are '''ND-100/CX''' machines
|-
| 330x || 3302 ND-100 Expansion System, 3304 ND-100/CE Expansion System
|-
| 339x || ND-110 Compact models 11 to 14: 3391-3394 ND-110, 3395-3398 ND-110/CX
|-
| 370x / 374x / 375x || Full-cabinet ND-110: 3701/3702 FTX packages, 3740 ND-110/CX system, 3750 ND-110/FTX
|}

Within a family, '''x1 marks FTX''' and '''x7 marks /CX'''. This is clean on the 5-series, where the ND-530 is 5351/5352 for FTX against 5371/5372 for /CX, and it carries into the 3-series where the ND-110 is 3750 for FTX against 3740 for /CX.

So the Compact model names form a sequence rather than a contradiction: ND-100 Compact models I to IV (326x, 1984), then ND-100 Compact models 11 to 14 (329x, 1987), then ND-110 Compact models 11 to 14 (339x). The A0/A1/B names used in the 308x and 309x blocks are not yet reconciled with these.

=== The older three-digit scheme ===

Before the four-digit codes there was a three-digit scheme, and ND's own generation program printed the values in its prompt. From a scanned SINGEN session in the SINTRAN order-form archive:

{{DocPreStart}}
     S i n g e n  f o r  S i n t r a n   V e r s i o n   J.
  Give CPU type: 100,500,502,900.    : 102
  Give CPU number:                   : 2954
  Give system name:                  : MOSS DAGBLAD A/S
{{DocPreEnd}}

The two schemes are separated by serial number: three-digit types appear with four-digit serials, four-digit types only with serials 16000 and above. In the 2711-record order archive the prefixes present are 100 (862 records), 102 (2), 500 (252), 502 (236), 503 (34), 504 (4), 900 (188) and 950 (1).

=== Disk interface on the Satellites ===

The ND-110 Satellite product sheet specifies a "Fixed Winchester disk drive with controller" on all four models, 60 MB on the S5 and S9 and 125 MB on the T9 and T17. In Norsk Data's vocabulary '''Winchester means ST-506''', not simply "a fixed disk": {{ND-doc|11.015.01}} is titled ''5 1/4 inch (ST506) & 8 inch Winchester Disk Controller'' and states that card '''3041''' "controls one or two Winchester Disk drives with the standard 5 1/4 inch interface connection ST506", while the ND-5000 ES System Administrator Guide writes the pairing as one term, "ST-506 (Winchester) disk".

So all four Satellite models shipped with '''ST-506 (MFM)''' disks. The S and T grades differ in capacity, not in interface.

Norsk Data kept the two interfaces on separate cards:

{| class="wikitable"
! Card !! Interface
|-
| 3041 || ST-506 Winchester, also prepared for ESDI
|-
| 3201 || SCSI and floppy, combined
|}

Beware when reading the card list of a preserved machine: at least one surviving ND-110 Satellite carries a 3201 SCSI/floppy card and a modern SCSI drive, but that machine was donated '''without a hard drive''' and the SCSI parts were fitted later. It shows that the ND-110 and ND-120 could take SCSI, not what the Satellite was delivered with.

Three cautions when reading a code off a machine:

* '''A plate records the machine as built, not as it stands.''' One machine listed as an ND-5830 carries plates reading 5430.19481, because it was later upgraded to a Rallar processor.
* '''Card part numbers overlap these codes and are a different set of numbers.''' The number 3095 is both a CPU type in the order manual and the part number of the ND-110/CX CPU card. It is not established whether that is deliberate.
* '''The {{ND-cmd|LIST-TITLE}} output changed between versions.''' On SINTRAN III/VSX it prints a full banner including CPU TYPE and CPU NUMBER lines. In the older NORD-10/S documentation the whole output is a single identification string such as "NORD-10/S - 781012".

== CPU type found by the operating system ==

A different value, the high byte of HWINFO(0), is what the kernel actually uses to decide how to behave. It is never asked for. The routine SYSEVAL works it out during start-up by testing the machine: it checks the status register for [[NORD-10]] against [[ND-100]], tries a shift to see whether floating point is 32 or 48 bits, and deliberately executes instructions such as BFILL, GECO and SLWCS to see which of them cause an internal interrupt on level 14.

{| class="wikitable"
! Value !! CPU
|-
| 0 / 1 || [[NORD-10]], 48-bit / 32-bit floating point
|-
| 2 / 3 || [[ND-100]], 48-bit / 32-bit floating point
|-
| 4 / 5 || [[ND-110]], 48-bit / 32-bit floating point
|-
| 6 / 7 || [[ND-120]], 48-bit / 32-bit floating point
|}

The low byte holds the instruction set, distinguishing the standard set from ND-100/CE, ND-100/CX, ND-110/CX and ND-120/CX. This value is tested in a dozen places in the kernel, including a fatal error at start-up if the machine is older than an ND-100/CX.

The VERSN instruction, opcode 140133, reads the microprogram version into HWINFO(1) on the ND-110 and ND-120.

== 5CPUTYPE, the coprocessor interface ==

A third value, 5CPUTYPE, records which kind of coprocessor is attached. It is found by probing the [[ND-100]] bus and seeing which interface answers, in the routine CH5CPUPRESENT.

* If the DMA status register on the '''PCB 3022''' bus interface answers without an input/output error, the value is set to OLD500, meaning an [[ND-500]].
* Otherwise, if the '''octobus''' status register at input/output address 100406 answers, the value is set to SAMSON, meaning an [[ND-5000]].
* If neither answers, no coprocessor is present.

The routine walks up to four CPU data fields, so that all processors in a multiprocessor system are found. It does not mix the two kinds: once a DMA interface has been found, the octobus test is skipped, and the other way round.

Note that this value identifies the '''interface''', not the processor. An ND-500/1 and an ND-500/2 both appear as OLD500, and both Samson and Rallar processors appear as SAMSON. Unlike the CPU type from the order form, this value is read later in several places to decide which transport to use.

== Does the CPU type do anything? ==

'''No effect on the running system has been found.'''

* The value has exactly one write and no reads anywhere in the available SINTRAN III sources, in both the J version and the L and M versions.
* The J version source comments the same word as "NOT USED".
* It leaves the kernel only through the {{ND-cmd|LIST-TITLE}} banner and through monitor call MON 262, which copies the whole system information array without inspecting any field.
* {{ND-doc|830053.3}} does not state anywhere that the CPU type changes the generated system, and the field sits outside the system parameters section that does.

The purpose appears to be '''identification rather than configuration'''. The order manual says of the CPU number that it "will identify the SINTRAN III later on when a new SINTRAN III needs to be installed", which fits a records purpose for both fields.

This is not a proof that nothing at all uses the value. The SINTRAN III kernel is what has been examined. The NEW-SYSTEM and S3-CONFIG programs, and layered products such as [[SIBAS]] and [[ND-COSMOS|COSMOS]], have not been examined, and any of them could read the value through MON 262. The number of legal users is held next to the CPU type in the same back wiring PROM, which makes a licence check the most obvious place to look.
